connect.apkGithub: Get the Android app on GitHub
connect.ios: iPhone: the app isn't on the App Store, so build it from source with Xcode. See the {link}.
connect.scanHow: In the app, open Settings › Scan to sign in and scan this QR code. The server address and token fill in by themselves
connect.unreachable: A phone can't reach this address
connect.badUrl: Write it as http://address:port or https://domain
connect.docker: The server runs in Docker and can't list this computer's addresses. Open this page on the computer by its LAN or Tailscale IP (port 8770 by default), or pick Enter it yourself
connect.bind: The server listens on {bind} only (HOST in .env), so other machines can't connect. For a phone to connect directly, set HOST=0.0.0.0 and restart
connect.manual: Can't scan? In the app, enter the server {address} and the token by hand
connect.connected: A phone is connected already. For a new or a second phone, just scan again
connect.first: Wear the recorder and see your first caption
connect.firstHow: Connect the recorder in the app (no recorder? the phone can record by itself), say something, and a few seconds later the caption shows up in Live captions
connect.diy: No recorder yet? Build one: the open-source {board}. Parts, wiring and the case are in {link}
connect.aiWhat: Let AI assistants such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Cherry Studio search the conversations, summaries and to-dos here, and mark to-dos Done or Wrong.
connect.aiUrl: The address is {url}, with the same token as the app.
connect.warnProvider: Once connected, the transcripts and summaries the AI looks up (what others said included) go to the AI provider you chose.
connect.warnTools: In sessions with this connection, don't auto-approve web or shell tools: words in a recording could be taken as instructions and use those tools to send content out.
connect.warnToken: The token can read and write all the data here. Keep it on your own computer only.
